metaData.originalTitle: Announcing ADK for Kotlin and ADK for Android 0.1.0: Building AI Agents on Android and Beyond
metaData.title: Announcing ADK for Kotlin and ADK for Android 0.1.0: Building AI Agents on Android and Beyond
metaData.oneSentenceSummary: Google announces the 0.1.0 release of the Agent Development Kit (ADK) for Kotlin and a specialized ADK for Android, enabling developers to build hybrid AI agents that orchestrate tasks between cloud models and on-device LLMs like Gemini Nano.
metaData.summary: This article from the Google Developers Blog announces the launch of version 0.1.0 of the Agent Development Kit (ADK) for Kotlin, along with a specialized ADK for Android library. The framework is designed to simplify the development of AI agents, particularly for hybrid cloud-edge scenarios. A key feature is hybrid orchestration, where a cloud-based agent can delegate specific tasks to sub-agents running entirely on-device using models like Gemini Nano. This approach enhances privacy by keeping sensitive data processing local while leveraging the reasoning power of cloud models. The article provides code examples for setting up agents, defining tools with annotations, and creating multi-agent systems. It also outlines the core feature set, including support for LLM-based, workflow-based, and custom agents, MCP and A2A integrations, session state management, and telemetry. The release is positioned as an experimental first step, with the goal of empowering developers to build intelligent, privacy-conscious applications on Android and beyond.

mainPoints.point: Google launches ADK for Kotlin and ADK for Android to simplify building hybrid AI agents.
mainPoints.explanation: The new SDKs allow developers to create agents that can orchestrate tasks between cloud-based LLMs and on-device models like Gemini Nano, managing complex orchestration, context, and error handling.

mainPoints.point: Hybrid orchestration enables privacy-preserving agent workflows.
mainPoints.explanation: A cloud orchestrator can delegate sensitive tasks, such as retrieving personal data from documents, to on-device sub-agents. This keeps private data on the device while using the cloud for complex reasoning.

mainPoints.point: The framework provides a comprehensive set of tools for agent development.
mainPoints.explanation: ADK supports LLM-based, workflow-based, and custom agents, along with function tools, MCP tools, A2A protocol, session state management, long-term memory, and OpenTelemetry for observability.

keyQuotes: ADK removes that friction by managing all the complex orchestration, context handling, and error handling for you.
You can use a cloud model as your main orchestrator, which can then offload specific tasks to sub-agents that run fully on-device.
By utilizing on-device models like Gemini Nano, you can create retrieval agents that access and parse documents locally, ensuring data never has to leave the hardware.

relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: Google I/O 2026 Developer keynote announces Gemini 3.5 models, the Antigravity 2.0 agent platform, and new tools for building Android and web apps with AI agents.

relatedArticles.title: State of the Claw
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: OpenClaw founder and OpenAI engineer Peter Steinberger discusses the unprecedented growth and security challenges of the OpenClaw project, shares his unique AI-assisted development workflow, and explores the evolving concept of 'engineer taste' in the AI era.

relatedArticles.title: Developer’s Guide to AI Agent Protocols
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: A comprehensive technical guide to the six essential protocols (MCP, A2A, UCP, AP2, A2UI, and AG-UI) that standardize how AI agents interact with data, other agents, commerce, payments, and user interfaces.

relatedArticles.title: Build Long-running AI agents that pause， resume， and never lose context with ADK
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This tutorial demonstrates how to build production-grade, long-running AI agents using Google's Agent Development Kit (ADK) that can pause, resume, and maintain context over days or weeks through durable state machines, persistent sessions, and event-driven resumption.

relatedArticles.title: Harness design for long-running application development
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article explores Anthropic's multi-agent harness design (Planner, Generator, Evaluator) for long-running autonomous coding, detailing how to overcome context anxiety and self-evaluation bias to build complex full-stack applications.

relatedArticles.title: Build Better AI Agents: 5 Developer Tips from the Agent Bake-Off
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article distills five key architectural patterns for building production-ready AI agents, based on lessons from Google's competitive Agent Bake-Off, emphasizing multi-agent workflows, modularity, multimodality, open protocols, and deterministic execution.

relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: Google announces the 1.0.0 release of the Agent Development Kit (ADK) for Java, providing a robust framework for building AI agents with grounding tools, plugin architecture, and human-in-the-loop workflows.
